# Jubilees Chapter 27 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Esau's fury; Jacob's dream at Bethel

---

**27:1** Esau burned with hatred toward Jacob over the stolen blessing. He told himself: "My father won't live forever. The moment he's gone, I'll kill Jacob."

**27:2** Word of Esau's intentions reached Rebekah. She quickly summoned Jacob and told him: "Your brother Esau is plotting to kill you.

**27:3** Listen to me carefully, son: get out of here now and run to my brother Laban in Haran.

**27:4** Stay with him until Esau's rage cools and he forgets what you did. When the time is right, I'll send for you. I can't lose both my sons at once."

**27:5** Rebekah went to Isaac and said: "Those Hittite daughters-in-law are making my life miserable. If Jacob marries another local woman like them, I don't think I can go on."

**27:6** Isaac called Jacob in, gave him his blessing, and issued him a firm charge: "Do not marry a Canaanite woman.

**27:7** Go to Paddan-aram, to your grandfather Bethuel's household, and find a wife there from your uncle Laban's daughters.

**27:8** May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful, and may your family grow into a great nation.

**27:9** May he pass on to you the blessing of Abraham my father — to you and your children after you — so that you inherit the land where we have lived as foreigners, the land God promised to Abraham."

**27:10** With that, Isaac sent Jacob on his way. He traveled to Paddan-aram and to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, who was Rebekah's brother — the mother of both Jacob and Esau.

**27:11** When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram specifically to find a non-Canaanite wife,

**27:12** And that Jacob had actually listened to his parents and gone —

**27:13** And when he realized how deeply the Canaanite women displeased his father —

**27:14** Esau went to the family of Ishmael and married Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, and the sister of Nebajoth. He added her to his existing wives.

**27:15** Jacob left Beer-sheba and headed toward Haran. When the sun went down he stopped at a certain place to sleep, using a stone as a pillow.

**27:16** That night he dreamed of a stairway reaching from earth to heaven, with God's angels moving up and down on it.

**27:17** The LORD himself stood at the top and spoke: "I am the LORD — the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. This land you're lying on I will give to you and your descendants.

**27:18** Your descendants will be as numerous as the dust of the earth. You will spread in every direction — west, east, north, south. Through you and your offspring, every family on earth will find blessing.

**27:19** I am with you. I will protect you wherever you go and bring you back to this land. I will never leave you until I have kept every promise I have made."

**27:20** Jacob woke up gasping: "The LORD is right here in this place — and I had no idea!"

**27:21** He was overcome with awe. "This place is terrifying," he said. "It's nothing less than the house of God — the very gateway to heaven."

**27:22** Early the next morning, Jacob took the stone he had slept on, stood it upright as a pillar, and poured oil over the top of it.

**27:23** He named the place Bethel — "House of God." Before that, the town had been called Luz.

**27:24** Then Jacob made a vow: "God, if you go with me on this journey and keep me safe — if you give me food and clothes and bring me home to my father —

**27:25** Then you, LORD, will be my God.

**27:26** This stone I've set up will mark your house. And everything you give me — I'll give you back a tenth."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering that captures the emotional arc — Esau's murderous rage, Rebekah's urgency, and Jacob's overwhelming encounter with the divine at Bethel. The dream sequence (vv.16-19) is rendered with immediacy; Jacob's vow (vv.24-26) preserves the conditional structure that is theologically significant.*
